The Advanced Concepts & Technologies Group (Group 39) is looking for exceptional engineers, scientists, and mathematicians who are excited to solve challenging problems. To improve operational effectiveness in rapidly evolving, complex threat environments, Group 39 conducts cutting-edge research and development in systems and architecture analysis; modeling and simulation; software and hardware prototyping and fielding; artificial intelligence; and signal processing. The group’s multidisciplinary team includes scientists and engineers with backgrounds in physics, mathematics, computer science, and engineering. Group 39 values inclusiveness, fosters mentoring at all levels, and promotes critical and innovative thinking to address the needs of the nation. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative team that supports professional growth and is dedicated to solving important national security challenges.

Job Description

The Advanced Concepts and Technologies Group is seeking an Associate Staff candidate to develop and apply artificial intelligence, modeling, and data-analysis methods for technology development and assessment. Our team works with government sponsors to understand complex operational and technical problems, develop new capabilities, and quantitatively evaluate emerging technologies and concepts.

The successful candidate will contribute across problem formulation, algorithm and software development, modeling, experimentation, and analysis. Working with government sponsors, mission subject-matter experts, scientists, and engineers, the candidate will translate open-ended questions into technical approaches and quantitative assessments. Work may involve deep learning, large language models, logic models, reinforcement learning, applied statistics, physics-based modeling, and analysis of complex structured and unstructured datasets. Depending on the problem, these methods may be applied through simulation, interactive environments, experimental prototypes, or other analysis tools.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Independently develop and apply AI, modeling, or analysis capabilities for technology development and assessment.Work with government sponsors and subject-matter experts to translate operational and technical questions into quantitative analyses, technical requirements, and evaluation criteria.Develop and evaluate AI/ML methods using deep learning, large language models, logic models, reinforcement learning, or related techniques.Develop and integrate statistical, physics-based, and data-driven models of complex systems and operations.Design and conduct quantitative studies and experiments, analyze complex structured and unstructured datasets, quantify uncertainty, and interpret technical and operational results.Develop software prototypes and analysis tools and contribute to software architecture, testing, verification, validation, documentation, version control, and code review.Take ownership of focused technical tasks and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to identify appropriate technical approaches and next steps.Communicate technical methods, assumptions, limitations, results, and recommendations through clear briefings, demonstrations, and written products for sponsor and technical audiences.


Requirements

Education / Qualifications

Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field. In lieu of a master’s degree, a bachelor’s degree with at least 2–3 years of directly relevant technical experience will be considered.Demonstrated programming ability in Julia, Python, or a similar scientific programming language.Experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computational decision modeling, including practical experience in at least one of the following areas: deep learning, large language models, logic models, or reinforcement learning.Demonstrated ability to formulate and solve complex, open-ended technical problems and independently develop software, models, algorithms, or analytical capabilities.Working knowledge of applied statistics, experimental design, and quantitative methods, including experience selecting appropriate methods and interpreting results.Experience analyzing complex, poorly structured, or unstructured datasets and extracting meaningful technical or operational insights.Strong written and oral technical communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical concepts, assumptions, methods, and results clearly.Ability to work independently, take ownership of technical tasks, and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams.Ability to rapidly develop expertise in new technical and mission areas.

rows.descriptionText:
Imagine if you had the skills, knowledge, and teammates to both understand the root of the world’s most pressing problems and build the technologies and companies best positioned to solve them. RA Capital has done exactly that for more than two decades, backing bold ideas in medicines to further human health and now expanding into Planetary Health to improve how efficiently we utilize the world’s precious resources.

RA Capital is among the leading providers of capital and services to the most promising innovators in the world. We invest flexibly—seed to IPO and beyond, anywhere in the world—with $10 B+ under management and a culture that prizes curiosity, rigor, and collaborative debate. We are investors who not only fund companies but get elbow deep in building them. From helping them recruit talent to helping them recruit patients for their studies to helping match them to strategic partners and even going to Washington to win reforms, RA Capital’s large team has people with nearly every relevant expertise one might need to turn an idea into a cure that actually helps people.

If you live for first-principles problem-solving with great colleagues, thrive on complexity, and want to do meaningful work that ripples across industries and ecosystems, you’ll feel at home at RA Capital. Here, questions are welcomed, ideas are tested, and victories are shared. Even our lawyers are creative and engaging. And don’t get us started on our compliance team’s wicked sense of humor; nothing about what we do is boring.

Are you ready to bring your creativity, discipline and collaborative spirit to help us invent the future? Join us and you’ll collaborate daily with investors, founders, physicians, biologists, engineers, economists, and reform advocates who think in systems and act with urgency.

Join us to invent a happier, healthier, more productive future - and have fun doing it.

Software Engineer, Data/AI – Healthcare Data & AI

About The Team

RA Capital’s Data Engineering team builds the enterprise data platform that powers research, investment, and operational workflows across the firm. Beyond traditional data pipelines, we are actively developing AI-native data access patterns that enable users to interact with complex healthcare datasets through LLM-powered, governed, and auditable interfaces.

Our work sits at the intersection of healthcare data, large-scale data engineering, and applied AI, with a strong emphasis on reliability, compliance, and production readiness.

About The Role

We are seeking an early-career software engineer to help build and operate AI-enabled data platforms and intelligent data workflows for healthcare data.

This role goes beyond traditional ETL. You will build healthcare data pipelines as well as AI-driven workflows and data applications that connect large language models with enterprise data and tools. This includes developing governed data access layers where LLMs translate user intent into structured queries and building agentic workflows that retrieve information, invoke tools, orchestrate multi-step tasks, and support self-service analytics, discovery, and decision-making.

Responsibilities

Design and maintain scalable, production-grade data pipelines for healthcare datasets, including claims and provider data. Build and optimize data models to support analytical and AI-driven workloads. Develop high-quality Python and SQL code for data standardization, reconciliation, validation, and application workflows. Build AI-powered data applications and agentic workflows that connect LLMs with enterprise data and internal tools, retrieve information, execute multi-step tasks, and automate data and research processes with appropriate guardrails. Build and improve AI-native data access frameworks, including LLM-to-SQL and LLM-to-GraphQL patterns and reusable interfaces for structured data access. Build backend services, APIs, and reusable software components that power data and AI applications. Develop evaluation and testing frameworks to measure the accuracy, reliability, and performance of LLM-powered and agentic workflows. Write automated tests and contribute to CI/CD, deployment, and production support for data and AI systems. Collaborate with AI/ML engineers, healthcare data vendors, and internal stakeholders to translate user needs into production-ready data and AI solutions. Implement monitoring, observability, and governance for data pipelines and AI workflows. Document data architectures, AI-enabled workflows, and production systems. 

Key Skills And Experience

Strong software engineering fundamentals and an interest in building production systems. Strong foundation in data engineering and data modeling. Proficiency in Python and SQL; experience with Spark and Databricks is preferred. Experience building or integrating APIs, services, or workflow-oriented applications. Hands-on experience with, or a strong interest in, LLM-powered applications, AI agents, or agentic workflows. Familiarity with LLM tool use, structured outputs, orchestration patterns, GraphQL, or other API-based data access methods. Experience working with healthcare or other regulated datasets is a plus. Strong communication, ownership, and collaboration skills. 

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. A master’s degree is preferred. Up to three years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or a related role. Must be based in the Boston area and available to work a hybrid schedule from our Boston office. Relocation assistance is not provided. Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

RA Capital Management is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Pay for this position will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, and current market conditions.

In addition to base salary (listed below), employees may be eligible for performance-based bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package that includes health insurance, retirement contributions, and paid time off.

The Institute for Protein Innovation (IPI)is a nonprofit research organization advancing protein science to accelerate research and improve human health. Founded in 2017 by Harvard Medical School professors Tim Springer and Andrew Kruse, we are located in Boston’s Longwood Medical Area.

The Institute’s three-pronged approach is to build protein tools, conduct related internal research, and develop educational programs for the protein science and broad biological research communities. With a significant endowment, IPI uniquely combines the freedom of academia with the high throughput and scale of industry to take on transformative projects. IPI has built a robust platform for discovering, developing, and distributing synthetic antibodies and other protein tools to share with the biomedical community. rows.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Organizational Memory (PhD Required)
rows.descriptionText:
Office Location: Wellesley, MA (3 days per week in the office)
Company OverviewAccrete is an agentic managed services company: we deliver the AI infrastructure and the AI workforce that does high-stakes, judgement-heavy work for government and enterprise clients — at the economics of software, not labor.At the core is Accrete’s Knowledge Engine, a dynamic context graph that captures an organization’s tacit knowledge, resolves data across silos, and builds a living, auditable ground truth. Expert agents reason against that ground truth to act on complex, high-stakes decisions — not just answer questions about them. From national security to commercial operations, Accrete delivers the work on one platform, with unlimited expert agents and expert judgement.
Job DescriptionWe are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to contribute to the research and development behind Accrete's context graphs — the intelligence layer the Knowledge Engine and its agents are built on.The work draws on knowledge representation, graph-based machine learning and information retrieval, combined with LLMs, to continuously construct, enrich, reason over, and maintain a structured picture of how an organization operates. Agentic systems are key: the graph and the agent topology built on top of it are designed together, since what agents need to retrieve and act on shapes how the graph is structured.The central challenge is to move past static knowledge graphs and conventional retrieval toward dynamic context graphs that capture how decisions get made and why — the actors, events, risks, and rules involved, the dependencies among them, and how all of it shifts over time. Much of what matters was never written down directly; it has to be reconstructed from the traces work leaves in tickets, threads, and meetings. In practice that means extraction from large volumes of heterogeneous data, resolving entities and relationships across sources, modeling provenance and uncertainty explicitly, and building graph structures agents can reason over reliably.This is an applied research role. Ideas become systems that run on real data at scale, developed alongside engineers and product teams. It also means taking evaluation seriously: there is no easy ground truth for whether a graph captured the right reasoning, and designing the benchmarks and adjudication methods that answer that question is part of the work, not an afterthought.
Key ResponsibilitiesConduct applied research focused on context graphs, knowledge representation, graph intelligence, and AI systems operating over complex, heterogeneous data.Develop algorithms and architectures for constructing and continuously updating dynamic context graphs from structured and unstructured data.Research methods for entity resolution, relationship extraction, event extraction, temporal reasoning, semantic linking, and knowledge discovery across disparate information sources.Develop graph-based representations of entities, relationships, events, decisions, processes, and organizational knowledge.Explore approaches for incorporating time, provenance, confidence, uncertainty, and source attribution into graph-based representations.Develop graph-based methods for supporting LLM reasoning, retrieval, planning, and agentic workflows.Research techniques for combining LLMs with structured graph representations to improve reasoning accuracy, grounding, and explainability.Design and evaluate graph algorithms, embeddings, retrieval methods, and machine learning approaches for discovering latent relationships and relevant context.Investigate methods for identifying changes, inconsistencies, gaps, and emerging patterns within evolving knowledge and context graphs.Develop prototypes and experimental systems and work with engineering teams to translate successful research into scalable production capabilities.Design benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for measuring graph quality, retrieval performance, reasoning accuracy, grounding, and system reliability.Stay current with advances in knowledge representation, graph ML, LLMs, information retrieval, databases, and related research areas.Contribute to technical strategy through research publications, patents, intellectual property, technical documentation, and mentorship.
Required QualificationsPh.D. in Computer Science, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computational Linguistics, Cognitive Science, or a related technical field, with a research focus in machine learning, NLP, knowledge representation, graph learning, or information retrieval.Research depth in at least two of the following, with working familiarity across the rest: knowledge representation and knowledge graphs; graph-based machine learning; information extraction and NLP; information retrieval and semantic search.A record of peer-reviewed publications at leading venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, KDD, WWW, or ISWC.Experience building extraction pipelines over unstructured and heterogeneous sources — entities, relationships, and events — including LLM-based extraction, retrieval-augmented generation, and embedding methods.Experience designing evaluation for problems without clean ground truth: benchmark construction, human annotation and adjudication protocols, agreement measurement, and baselines strong enough that beating them is meaningful.Strong programming and system-building skills in Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience using graph databases such as Neo4j and graph learning frameworks such as PyTorch Geometric or DGL.Demonstrated ability to turn research ideas into working systems — research code others can run, open-source contributions, or systems that outlived a single paper's experiments.Ability to formulate research questions independently under ambiguity, and to communicate technical work clearly to research, engineering, and product audiences.
Preferred QualificationsFamiliarity with cognitive or organizational memory theory (episodic/semantic memory, consolidation, transactive memory, tacit knowledge) and interest in translating it into computational representations of how organizations retain and lose knowledge.Prior industry research internships or post-doctoral experience, particularly applied work on real data at scale.Experience with multi-agent systems built over structured knowledge: agent topology and orchestration, tool interface design, and evaluation of agent trajectories.Experience with dynamic or temporal knowledge graphs, and with temporal graph learning architectures.Experience with schema and ontology evolution in knowledge systems — versioning, migration, and re-extraction as representations change.Experience with belief revision and knowledge maintenance: handling contradictory evidence, retiring stale assertions, and modeling when something was true separately from when the system learned it.Experience adapting or distilling open-weight models to encode domain knowledge, including fine-tuning and knowledge distillation.Experience applying research in enterprise, intelligence, or defense settings, where outputs must be grounded, attributable, and correctable.Salary Range: $160k-$210kThe salary range provided reflects the estimated compensation for this role based on the expected qualifications and experience level. The final offer may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and alignment with role requirements.

Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account.

HHMI is focused on supporting and moving science forward in a variety of different ways ranging from conducting basic biomedical research, empowering educators, inspiring students, developing the next generation of scientists – even stretching into film and media production. Our Headquarters is in the greater Washington, DC metro area and is home to over 300 employees with expertise in investments, communications, digital production, biomedical sciences, and everything in between. The work housed here supports and augments the groundbreaking research conducted in HHMI labs across the nation. As HHMI scientists continue to push boundaries in laboratories and classrooms, you can be sure that your contributions while working here are making a difference.

We are always open to finding self-motivated and highly organized Postdoctoral Scientist candidates for potential opportunities within our labs in the greater Boston area.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. You will be contacted by a member of our Recruitment team if your skills and experience appear to be a match when a role opens.

The Postdoctoral Scientist performs a variety of research and/or laboratory tasks and experiments under general supervision. Analyzes data and records the results and conclusions of laboratory experiments. Interprets analytical data and prepares research reports. May assist in the establishment of experimental protocols. Postdoc appointments are tied to a research program advised by the Investigator.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Performs research and/or development in collaboration with others for projects. Makes detailed observations, analyzes data, and interprets resultsExercises technical discretion in the design, execution, and interpretation of experiments that contribute to project strategies. Prepares technical reports, summaries, protocols, and quantitative analyses. Maintains familiarity with current scientific literatureContributes to project process within their scientific field. Investigates, builds, and develops new methods and technologies for project advancement. Maintains high level of professional expertise through familiarity with scientific literature. May participate in scientific conferences and contribute to scientific journals. Uses professional concepts in accordance with HHMI’s objectives to tackle complex problems in creative and effective ways. May determine methods and procedures on new assignments and may provide mentorship to staff in the laboratory. 

Qualifications

Education

Ph.D. degree in a scientific field or MD degree

Skills And Abilities

Proven understanding of scientific principlesExercises independent judgment in developing methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for acquiring resultsAbility to perform highly complex experiments with high levels of reliability and accuracy within time constraintsOperational knowledge of sophisticated lab equipmentAbility to provide work and supervise directions to othersAbility to initiate and compose communications for various purposes in an appropriate styleAbility to work successfully within a collaborative and congenial environment and foster this ability in others. Ability to review goals, analyze processes vital to achieve those goals, and develop techniques and systems required to meet those goals. Often explores new areas and seeks opportunities to apply new knowledge to work. 

Physical Requirements

Remaining in a normal seated or standing position for extended periods of time; reaching and grasping by extending hand(s) or arm(s); dexterity to manipulate objects with fingers, for example using a keyboard; communication skills using the spoken word; ability to see and hear within normal parameters; ability to move about workspace. The position requires mobility, including the ability to move materials weighing up to several pounds (such as a laptop computer or tablet).

Persons with disabilities may be able to perform the essential duties of this position with reasonable accommodation. Requests for reasonable accommodation will be evaluated on an individual basis.

This job description sets forth the job’s principal duties, responsibilities, and requirements; it should not be construed as an exhaustive statement, however. Unless they begin with the word “may,” the Essential Duties and Responsibilities described above are “essential functions” of the job, as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act.

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

This is an opportunity for a motivated Operations Research Analyst to join MITRE’s Operations Analysis department. We are a large group of over 60 operations research professionals, including over 20 PhDs, who provide thought leadership on a variety of strategic and technical issues, perform analysis that enable our sponsors to make more effective decisions, lead internal research and development activities to bring new technical capabilities into the public sector, and serve as trusted third-party advisors to government sponsors on a variety of technical topics.

In short, we apply our problem-solving skills to complex interdisciplinary problems that occur within or at the intersection of organizations, operations, and technology. We support sponsor projects across the defense and public sectors including homeland defense, military logistics, radio-spectrum frequency management, health care delivery, cybersecurity analytics, fraud detection, satellite planning, homeland security and civilian aviation. If you are passionate about project-based analytical work in the public interest, you have found the right place.

The Advanced Concepts & Technologies Group (Group 39) is looking for exceptional engineers, scientists, and mathematicians who are excited to solve challenging problems. To improve operational effectiveness in rapidly evolving, complex threat environments, Group 39 conducts cutting-edge research and development in systems and architecture analysis; modeling and simulation; software and hardware prototyping and fielding; artificial intelligence; and signal processing. The group’s multidisciplinary team includes scientists and engineers with backgrounds in physics, mathematics, computer science, and engineering. Group 39 values inclusiveness, fosters mentoring at all levels, and promotes critical and innovative thinking to address the needs of the nation. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative team that supports professional growth and is dedicated to solving important national security challenges.

Job Description

The Advanced Concepts and Technologies Group is seeking an Associate Staff candidate to develop and apply artificial intelligence, modeling, and data-analysis methods for technology development and assessment. Our team works with government sponsors to understand complex operational and technical problems, develop new capabilities, and quantitatively evaluate emerging technologies and concepts.

The successful candidate will contribute across problem formulation, algorithm and software development, modeling, experimentation, and analysis. Working with government sponsors, mission subject-matter experts, scientists, and engineers, the candidate will translate open-ended questions into technical approaches and quantitative assessments. Work may involve deep learning, large language models, logic models, reinforcement learning, applied statistics, physics-based modeling, and analysis of complex structured and unstructured datasets. Depending on the problem, these methods may be applied through simulation, interactive environments, experimental prototypes, or other analysis tools.

Requirements

Education / Qualifications

Boston University invites applications for a faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Department of Earth & Environment. This tenure-track position in Climate Data Science, beginning on July 1, 2027, is part of the ongoing cluster hire in Environmental Data Science and complements faculty searches within the Faculty of Computing and Data Science. 
We particularly welcome candidates whose research focuses on the physical basis of climate, climate variability, and climate change, and who employ data science methodologies to deepen our understanding of how the climate system is changing and how these changes affect the global environment. Areas of interest include—but are not limited to—the changing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events; interactions between the atmosphere and terrestrial, oceanic, biospheric, and cryospheric systems; and improved understanding of Earth system predictability at seasonal, decadal, and longer time scales. We envision this position playing a central role in connecting and enhancing existing departmental strengths in climate-related research and teaching, including terrestrial and marine biogeosciences, land surface and coastal processes, paleoclimatology, energy and economic policy, and environmental sustainability. Timeframe{{:}} Summer (May-Aug 2027)

Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment.

Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity!

What We Need

Symbotic is looking for an applied scientist intern with a passion for multi-agent planning to improve the performance and reliability of our systems as we rapidly scale our product and organization. The Robot Routing team plans highly efficient, collision-free paths between the storage structure and the inbound/outbound cells of our system for dozens of robots traversing the transfer deck. The right candidate is excited about concepts like deadlock resolution and time-space reservations. This is a hybrid position based at our headquarters in Wilmington, MA.

What You’ll Do

Identify high-impact scenarios where AI Planning and machine learning can be applied to optimize the Symbotic robotics software. Adapt state-of-the-art approaches or develop high-performance algorithms to solve real-world multi-robot problems. Conduct simulations and experiments to validate the performance of the multi-robot algorithms. Present results in verbal and written communications internally, and in top-tier academic venues. 

What You’ll Need

Pursuing PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Proficiency in one or more general-purpose programming languages{{:}} C++, Python, Java, or C#. Strong research background in combinatorial optimization, Robotics planning, multi-robot systems, or machine learning. Publications at high-impact conferences/journals (e.g., CoRL, ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, RSS, ICRA, IROS, RAL, AAAI, ICAPS, IJCAI, JAIR, etc.) on some of the aforementioned topics.

Position Description

CGI is seeking an AI Automation Engineer to design, deploy, and support intelligent AI agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio that transform manual tasks and streamline business processes. In this highly collaborative role, you’ll work closely with the AI Architect and business stakeholders to identify process challenges, turn ideas into practical AI-powered solutions, and measure their adoption and business impact.

This position can be performed near any CGI office (preference in MA)

Your future duties and responsibilities

 Requirements discovery: Work with the AI Architect and business users to understand manual workflows, identify automation candidates, and define agent scope and success criteria. Agent development: Build agents in Copilot Studio, including topics, prompts, knowledge sources, actions, and conversation flows. Workflow automation: Connect agents to systems using Power Automate, connectors, and APIs (e.g., SharePoint, Teams, Outlook, Dataverse, Excel, ServiceNow, internal apps). Prompt and knowledge design: Write and refine instructions, ground agents on enterprise content, and tune responses for accuracy and consistency. Testing and quality: Test agents for accuracy, edge cases, and failure handling. Validate with business users before release. Deployment and governance: Follow architect defined standards for security, data access, DLP, environment management (dev/test/prod), and responsible AI. Usage tracking and reporting: Monitor agent adoption, volume, resolution rates, and time/effort saved. Build simple dashboards (Power BI or Copilot Studio analytics) and report progress to leadership. Continuous improvement: Review feedback and usage data, then iterate on agents to improve performance and expand coverage. Documentation and enablement: Maintain agent documentation, runbooks, and user guides. Train business users on adoption.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

 Must have at least 6 + years of experience as a full stack developer with Python or similar language 3+ years in automation, software, or solutions engineering Hands on experience with Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Platform (Power Automate, Power Apps, Dataverse) - Mandatory Working knowledge of generative AI concepts: LLMs, prompt engineering, grounding/RAG, and agent limitations Ability to translate business processes into automated workflows Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with non technical stakeholders

Desired Qualifications

 Microsoft certifications (PL 200, PL 400, AI 900, AI 102) Experience with Azure AI services (Azure OpenAI, AI Foundry, AI Search) Familiarity with agent frameworks beyond Copilot Studio Basic Python or JavaScript for custom actions Power BI for usage and ROI reporting Experience in healthcare, insurance, or other regulated industries

rows.title: AI/ML Engineer - Associate Staff
rows.descriptionText:
The Advanced Concepts & Technologies Group (Group 39) is looking for exceptional engineers, scientists, and mathematicians who are excited to solve challenging problems. To improve operational effectiveness in rapidly evolving, complex threat environments, Group 39 conducts cutting-edge research and development in systems and architecture analysis; modeling and simulation; software and hardware prototyping and fielding; artificial intelligence; and signal processing. The group’s multidisciplinary team includes scientists and engineers with backgrounds in physics, mathematics, computer science, and engineering. Group 39 values inclusiveness, fosters mentoring at all levels, and promotes critical and innovative thinking to address the needs of the nation. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative team that supports professional growth and is dedicated to solving important national security challenges.

Job Description

The Advanced Concepts and Technologies Group is seeking an Associate Staff candidate to develop and apply artificial intelligence, modeling, and data-analysis methods for technology development and assessment. Our team works with government sponsors to understand complex operational and technical problems, develop new capabilities, and quantitatively evaluate emerging technologies and concepts.

The successful candidate will contribute across problem formulation, algorithm and software development, modeling, experimentation, and analysis. Working with government sponsors, mission subject-matter experts, scientists, and engineers, the candidate will translate open-ended questions into technical approaches and quantitative assessments. Work may involve deep learning, large language models, logic models, reinforcement learning, applied statistics, physics-based modeling, and analysis of complex structured and unstructured datasets. Depending on the problem, these methods may be applied through simulation, interactive environments, experimental prototypes, or other analysis tools.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Independently develop and apply AI, modeling, or analysis capabilities for technology development and assessment.Work with government sponsors and subject-matter experts to translate operational and technical questions into quantitative analyses, technical requirements, and evaluation criteria.Develop and evaluate AI/ML methods using deep learning, large language models, logic models, reinforcement learning, or related techniques.Develop and integrate statistical, physics-based, and data-driven models of complex systems and operations.Design and conduct quantitative studies and experiments, analyze complex structured and unstructured datasets, quantify uncertainty, and interpret technical and operational results.Develop software prototypes and analysis tools and contribute to software architecture, testing, verification, validation, documentation, version control, and code review.Take ownership of focused technical tasks and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to identify appropriate technical approaches and next steps.Communicate technical methods, assumptions, limitations, results, and recommendations through clear briefings, demonstrations, and written products for sponsor and technical audiences.


Requirements

Education / Qualifications

Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field. In lieu of a master’s degree, a bachelor’s degree with at least 2–3 years of directly relevant technical experience will be considered.Demonstrated programming ability in Julia, Python, or a similar scientific programming language.Experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computational decision modeling, including practical experience in at least one of the following areas: deep learning, large language models, logic models, or reinforcement learning.Demonstrated ability to formulate and solve complex, open-ended technical problems and independently develop software, models, algorithms, or analytical capabilities.Working knowledge of applied statistics, experimental design, and quantitative methods, including experience selecting appropriate methods and interpreting results.Experience analyzing complex, poorly structured, or unstructured datasets and extracting meaningful technical or operational insights.Strong written and oral technical communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical concepts, assumptions, methods, and results clearly.Ability to work independently, take ownership of technical tasks, and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams.Ability to rapidly develop expertise in new technical and mission areas.


Desired Qualifications

Software engineering experience, including software architecture, modular and extensible design, automated testing, version control, code review, and technical documentation.Experience applying AI/ML, modeling, or data analysis to technology development, system assessment, or decision support.Experience with formal or logic-based modeling approaches, such as PDDL, signal temporal logic, automated planning, rule-based systems, or related methods.Experience developing visualizations, user interfaces, or interactive tools for complex technical systems, including simulations, analytical applications, or serious games.Familiarity with Department of War missions, operations, systems, or technologies.Background in physics-based modeling, particularly radar systems, sensor performance, detection, tracking, or radio-frequency propagation.Experience with Monte Carlo simulation, experimental design, uncertainty quantification, and/or sensitivity analysis.Experience with agent-based models, decision-support tools, human-machine teaming, or autonomous decision-making systems.Experience with high-performance, parallel, distributed, or GPU computing.Experience leading focused technical tasks or working directly with government sponsors.Active Secret clearance.

rows.title: Software Engineer, AI-Native Products
rows.descriptionText:
Misneach Means CourageMisneach (MISH-nock) is an Irish word for courage, spirit, and resolve. We chose it because building something from nothing takes all three, and because it is the quality we look for in every founder we back and every person we hire. We are building a Founder Propulsion Platform for early-stage founders. We pair capital with embedded AI infrastructure, operating systems, commercial expertise, and hands-on execution, so founders can move with speed and leverage from day one.We believe the early-stage model has not kept pace with what founders need. Capital matters, but capital alone does not build companies. We are building everything around it, and we are doing it as a small team that uses AI to operate like a much larger one. Our working goal is simple: a team of 10 that does the work of 30.That is where you come in.
The RoleWe are hiring a Software Engineer to build AI-native products. The title describes the work. It does not describe the person we are looking for, and we care about the person at least as much as the skill set. Skills can be learned in weeks. The mindset that makes someone want to learn them is much harder to find.You will join a small team building Misneach’s AI platform in real time. You will ship products, agents, workflows, and infrastructure used by our team and by the founders we back. You will also take what we build into portfolio companies and see firsthand where AI creates real operating leverage and where it does not.Nothing here arrives as a neatly packaged ticket. You will work close to the people with the problem, figure out what needs to be solved, prototype fast, and own what you build all the way into production.
What’s Already BuiltYou will not start from a blank repo. The foundation is in place: a shared platform of services for identity, authentication, payments, workflows, and AI agents. Three products already run on it: a go-to-market platform for founders, an AI operating system that runs our own investment workflow, and a third founder-facing product now moving into production.You will build what comes next on the same foundation. Our standard: a feature is done when its checks pass on real production data and stay green, not when the code merges.
What You’ll BuildYour work spans three areas, with room to lean into your strengths.Platform and product. You will build and ship the founder-facing platform and our AI Marketplace, working across product discovery, user experience, data models, integrations, backend services, and deployment.AI systems and agents. You will design the intelligence underneath the platform: agents, retrieval and search, knowledge systems, recommendations, evaluations, workflows, and orchestration.Founder deployments and internal systems. You will turn what we learn into working systems. Some of that lives inside portfolio companies, where a capability can change how a five-person team operates. Some of it lives inside Misneach, where it lets our own team punch far above its size.
We work AI-native. You will use Claude and other modern tools heavily every day, and you will bring the judgment to know when generated output is useful, when it is not, and what belongs in production.
Is This You?Read this section closely. It matters more to us than the skills list that follows. If most of it reads like a description of you, we want to meet you, even if your resume does not check every box.
HOW YOU THINKYou have the learner gene. You get restless when nothing on your plate is new. When a model, framework, or protocol ships that you have never touched, you open a terminal that evening, and by the end of the week you can explain where it is useful and where it falls apart. You enjoy the process of getting good at something as much as being good at it.You see a blank canvas and get excited. Where others ask for a spec, you see possibilities. You sketch three ways a problem could be solved, pick the one worth testing first, and turn an open question into something people can react to. You would rather be early and occasionally wrong than late and safe.
HOW YOU BUILDYou build your own ideas, not just the ones handed to you. You spot a problem nobody assigned, build a working version over a few days, and walk in with “I had an idea, I built it, let me show you how it works.” You would rather show up with a working prototype than a proposal asking for permission.You are a finisher, not a demo builder. A demo that works once on your laptop is where your interest starts. You are not satisfied until the system handles messy real-world inputs, fails gracefully, has evals that tell you when it degrades, and is used by someone who has never met you.You are a force multiplier. When you see the same task done by hand three times, you are already turning it into an agent, a workflow, or a reusable component. You measure your work by how much more the people around you can do because of it. That is how a team of 10 does the work of 30.
HOW YOU WORK WITH OTHERSYou run on autonomy and stay tightly connected. A founder describes a loose problem on Monday, and you come back Wednesday with a working prototype and the three questions that actually matter. You do not need a plan handed to you, and you never confuse autonomy with working alone: you share rough work early, ask for hard critique, and count it as a win when a teammate ships faster because of something you built.You are a translator. You can sit with a founder who has never heard the term retrieval-augmented generation, find the real problem underneath the request, and explain the tradeoffs in plain language. You are as comfortable in a room with operators and investors as you are in a pull request.
HOW YOU HANDLE THE HARD PARTSYou have the courage to jump in. Faced with a problem nobody on the team has solved and no playbook to follow, you do not wait for perfect information. You build something small, test it, learn from it, and try again. Being wrong on Tuesday does not bother you as long as you are less wrong by Thursday.You stay steady when the ground moves. Monday is the platform. Wednesday a portfolio company has an urgent problem. Friday a model provider changes something you depend on. You recalibrate without drama, keep a clear view of what matters most this week, and keep shipping.
What You’ll Likely BringWe are less interested in years on a resume than in evidence of how you build. Most people who thrive here have shipped real software for a year or more, often with serious hands-on building well before that. Here is the kind of evidence we look for.You have shipped software people actually use. Professional work, a substantial co-op or internship, an open-source contribution, or a product you built on your own all count. We want to see something that left your laptop.You have built with LLMs past the tutorial stage. You have put an agent, a retrieval system, or an AI workflow in front of real users, and you can tell us what broke and what you changed.Your fundamentals are solid. You are comfortable across Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, APIs, integrations, data models, and modern application architecture, and you pick up what you do not know quickly.You use AI tools with judgment. Claude and similar tools are part of how you work every day, and you know how to evaluate what they produce rather than accept it.You have built from zero before. A startup, a 0 to 1 project, or a side product where you had to figure out what to build as well as how to build it.You care about the user and the business. You want to understand why a problem matters before you decide how to solve it.
This Is Probably Not You IfYou want a long backlog of well-defined tickets and a clear spec before you start.You prefer to go deep on one narrow part of a large system for years.You consider a project finished when the demo works.You would rather wait for the right answer than learn your way toward it.
None of these are flaws. They describe a different kind of job, and there are great companies built around them. This is not one of them.
Why This Role Is DifferentYou will get exposure few engineers get this early in a career. You will harden and extend a platform that is already running, while working alongside founders who are building their own companies from the ground up. Product decisions, customer problems, go-to-market questions, and the realities of company-building will all be in front of you.Some weeks you will be deep in the Misneach platform. Other weeks you will spot an opportunity inside a portfolio company and help turn an idea into something working.We are early enough that you will shape how we build as well as what we build: our architecture, our tooling, our product practices, and our approach to deploying AI across everything we touch.Some of what we build for ourselves or our portfolio companies may turn out to have real market potential. Misneach also incubates companies, so when something built here shows that kind of promise, it has a path to become more than an internal tool.
What We OfferBase salary of $130K–$180K, depending on experience, plus an annual performance-based bonus targeted at 20% of base salary, based on individual and company performance.Fully covered medical for you and your dependents.Company-paid dental, vision, life and AD&D, and long-term disability coverage.401(k) retirement plan.Flexible PTO, company holidays, and company-wide remote weeks.Health Care and Dependent Care FSA options.MBTA commuter benefit.Primarily in-person work from our Boston office, with flexibility.
At this time, we are unable to sponsor employment visas for this role.How to ApplyApply through LinkedIn Easy Apply, or email recruiting@misneach.ai with the subject line “Software Engineer, AI-Native Products Application.”More than a resume, we want to see something you built. Send a GitHub repo, a live product, a demo, a side project, or an open-source contribution.

rows.title: Software Engineer, Data/AI
rows.descriptionText:
Imagine if you had the skills, knowledge, and teammates to both understand the root of the world’s most pressing problems and build the technologies and companies best positioned to solve them. RA Capital has done exactly that for more than two decades, backing bold ideas in medicines to further human health and now expanding into Planetary Health to improve how efficiently we utilize the world’s precious resources.

RA Capital is among the leading providers of capital and services to the most promising innovators in the world. We invest flexibly—seed to IPO and beyond, anywhere in the world—with $10 B+ under management and a culture that prizes curiosity, rigor, and collaborative debate. We are investors who not only fund companies but get elbow deep in building them. From helping them recruit talent to helping them recruit patients for their studies to helping match them to strategic partners and even going to Washington to win reforms, RA Capital’s large team has people with nearly every relevant expertise one might need to turn an idea into a cure that actually helps people.

If you live for first-principles problem-solving with great colleagues, thrive on complexity, and want to do meaningful work that ripples across industries and ecosystems, you’ll feel at home at RA Capital. Here, questions are welcomed, ideas are tested, and victories are shared. Even our lawyers are creative and engaging. And don’t get us started on our compliance team’s wicked sense of humor; nothing about what we do is boring.

Are you ready to bring your creativity, discipline and collaborative spirit to help us invent the future? Join us and you’ll collaborate daily with investors, founders, physicians, biologists, engineers, economists, and reform advocates who think in systems and act with urgency.

Join us to invent a happier, healthier, more productive future - and have fun doing it.

Software Engineer, Data/AI – Healthcare Data & AI

About The Team

RA Capital’s Data Engineering team builds the enterprise data platform that powers research, investment, and operational workflows across the firm. Beyond traditional data pipelines, we are actively developing AI-native data access patterns that enable users to interact with complex healthcare datasets through LLM-powered, governed, and auditable interfaces.

Our work sits at the intersection of healthcare data, large-scale data engineering, and applied AI, with a strong emphasis on reliability, compliance, and production readiness.

About The Role

We are seeking an early-career software engineer to help build and operate AI-enabled data platforms and intelligent data workflows for healthcare data.

This role goes beyond traditional ETL. You will build healthcare data pipelines as well as AI-driven workflows and data applications that connect large language models with enterprise data and tools. This includes developing governed data access layers where LLMs translate user intent into structured queries and building agentic workflows that retrieve information, invoke tools, orchestrate multi-step tasks, and support self-service analytics, discovery, and decision-making.

Responsibilities

Design and maintain scalable, production-grade data pipelines for healthcare datasets, including claims and provider data. Build and optimize data models to support analytical and AI-driven workloads. Develop high-quality Python and SQL code for data standardization, reconciliation, validation, and application workflows. Build AI-powered data applications and agentic workflows that connect LLMs with enterprise data and internal tools, retrieve information, execute multi-step tasks, and automate data and research processes with appropriate guardrails. Build and improve AI-native data access frameworks, including LLM-to-SQL and LLM-to-GraphQL patterns and reusable interfaces for structured data access. Build backend services, APIs, and reusable software components that power data and AI applications. Develop evaluation and testing frameworks to measure the accuracy, reliability, and performance of LLM-powered and agentic workflows. Write automated tests and contribute to CI/CD, deployment, and production support for data and AI systems. Collaborate with AI/ML engineers, healthcare data vendors, and internal stakeholders to translate user needs into production-ready data and AI solutions. Implement monitoring, observability, and governance for data pipelines and AI workflows. Document data architectures, AI-enabled workflows, and production systems. 

Key Skills And Experience

Strong software engineering fundamentals and an interest in building production systems. Strong foundation in data engineering and data modeling. Proficiency in Python and SQL; experience with Spark and Databricks is preferred. Experience building or integrating APIs, services, or workflow-oriented applications. Hands-on experience with, or a strong interest in, LLM-powered applications, AI agents, or agentic workflows. Familiarity with LLM tool use, structured outputs, orchestration patterns, GraphQL, or other API-based data access methods. Experience working with healthcare or other regulated datasets is a plus. Strong communication, ownership, and collaboration skills. 

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. A master’s degree is preferred. Up to three years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or a related role. Must be based in the Boston area and available to work a hybrid schedule from our Boston office. Relocation assistance is not provided. Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship. 

Compensation

RA Capital Management is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Pay for this position will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, and current market conditions.

In addition to base salary (listed below), employees may be eligible for performance-based bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package that includes health insurance, retirement contributions, and paid time off.

Total Rewards

rows.title: Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Foods you love. Brands you trust. And a career that empowers you to grow.

At Nestlé USA, we’re all working towards the same goal – to delight and deliver for our consumers. With a rich portfolio of beloved brands, including DiGiorno, Toll House, and Coffee mate, in 97% of U.S. households, we have a unique opportunity – and responsibility – to be there for every moment in our consumers’ lives.

Joining Nestlé means becoming part of an inclusive workplace that inspires innovation, encourages strategic thinking and creativity, and celebrates your achievements. No matter where you work within the organization, you are empowered to challenge the status quo, embrace risk-taking, and pioneer new ideas. Our supportive and collaborative environment encourages bold ambitions and continuous learning so that everyone can grow and thrive.

This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship.

Reporting into the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager within the Commercial Excellence organization, the Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst will be a crucial addition to a team whose mission is to implement an adaptive, industry-leading Social Intelligence capability into Nestle USA that is considered a trusted source of actionable, real-time insight into consumer perception & culture. The Social Intelligence capability has been built to support stakeholders across Brand Marketing, Consumer & Marketplace Insights, Social Strategy & Community, Foresight, Innovation, Category Strategy, Corporate Communication and other teams; ultimately, our goal is to fully embed the capability throughout Nestle USA and empower stakeholders across every department to act upon real-time social media insights.

Additionally, the Senior Analyst will be a crucial member of the emerging cross-functional capability of AI Readiness by supporting LLM Listening & Visibility analysis, including tool implementation & governance, stakeholder support and incorporation into Social Intelligence analysis deliverables.

After supporting the final stages of the Social Intelligence capability’s implementation across Nestle USA, and the incorporation of LLM Listening into our processes, the Digital & Social Intelligence Senior Analyst’s role will focus on robust stakeholder relationship building with teams across the organization, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders to provide consistent, timely & actionable insights for our brands, while forging a continuous stakeholder feedback loop on our offerings. The insights the Analyst will deliver will originate from both cadenced and ad-hoc research requests, while the feedback the Senior Analyst gathers will inform how we optimize & evolve the Digital & Social Intelligence capability over time using ever-evolving AI-driven technology.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to balance supporting stakeholders by fulfilling research requests using our best-in-class technology stack, while also training the stakeholders to be able to leverage the technology to find insights on their own. This balance will allow the Senior Analyst, along with the rest of the Digital & Social Intelligence team, to focus our efforts on the most important in-depth analysis the organization needs, while empowering our stakeholders to conduct their own light monitoring of day-to-day digital & social insights questions. The role will work in collaboration with other stakeholders within the Center of Demand Generation, including but not limited to Foresight, Consumer Insights, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Shopper Insights and Innovation, to provide capabilities and services that consistently identify, generate & distribute actionable & timely insights to Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand Marketing teams.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to work with our stakeholder teams to understand Nestle USA’s business objectives and brand strategies across a wide variety of product categories such as coffee, coffee creamer, chocolate & desserts, frozen meals, pizza, snacking, baking ingredients, noodles and sauces. Day-to-day activities vary given the nature of our business, but the Senior Analyst can expect to balance answering business questions through in-depth analysis using multiple technologies, collaborating with stakeholders in key meetings, developing and executing self-service training programs, identifying & helping implement new technology features, working with vendors and attending leadership presentations.

On top of the various product categories we support and the multiple technologies we use, the world of social media and AI-driven technology changes rapidly. Therefore, a balance of technical skill, strategic thinking, proactivity, flexibility and a solution-seeking attitude is crucial for success in this role.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Social Listening, LLM Listening & Related Social Media Research, including Presentation to Stakeholders. Leverage Nestle USA’s Digital & Social Intelligence technology stack to conduct in-depth research about our brands, competitors, product categories and relevant cultural trends, using the insights to deliver a persuasive & visual story to stakeholders that drives action within their key initiatives. This includes navigating technology that handles every facet of Digital & Social Intelligence, such as social listening, ratings & reviews listening, LLM Listening / GEO / AEO, emerging trend identification, social audience persona building, influencer evaluation and owned content performance benchmarking. Where applicable, this also includes combining findings with other data sources outside of Social Intelligence, often via collaboration with our broader Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics and Consumer Insights teams, to provide comprehensive analysis to the stakeholder. Stakeholder Training & Guidance. Assist in the development and execution of training programs, including building training material, leading office hours and sitting one-on-one with stakeholders to guide them through use cases for social listening & social intelligence that build confidence in their ability to navigate the technology to find insights.Stakeholder Request Management. Assist the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager in managing an analysis request queue, which assigns priority to each ad-hoc social research request based on impact to the business, level of effort and urgency. This includes keeping track of stakeholder check-in cadences to ensure the Digital & Social Intelligence team is consistently engaging each key stakeholder group. Tool Output Scanning & Insights Identification. Review the automated reporting outputs from the various tools, including weekly/bi-weekly/monthly AI-driven reports and real-time email alerts, to ensure continuous improvement in the quality of the automated outputs while also mining for actionable insights that need to be flagged to our stakeholders for further discussion & potential action.Tool Maintenance & Governance. Assist in the day-to-day management of the tools, from user access to dashboard/report quality, flagging issues or needs to the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager while collaborating with 3rd party and shared service support teams. Vendor Collaboration. Partnering with analysts from 3rd parties and shared service teams on key research projects and key feature advancements, as well as brainstorming and providing feedback to tool providers on ideal features and functionality that maximize actionability. 
REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL:

Bachelor's degree in marketing, market research, analytics, communications, business, economics, or related field3-5 years of experience in social listening and additional social research, including in-tool navigational experience and strategic storytelling of analysis results.3-5 years in a strategic role working with data analytics, with a focus on developing strong dashboards and/or other automatically refreshable visualizations that empower stakeholders to quickly identify key takeaways from data
DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

Experience using Talkwalker, Nichefire, Yogi, Audiense, Creator IQ, Sprinklr or similar tools throughout every part of the process: query building, dashboard visualization, automated report building and ultimately in-depth analysis of key takeawaysFamiliarity with the emerging LLM Listening & Visibility / GEO / AEO analysis space, including tools such as ProfoundStrong understanding of how AI can be used to support Digital & Social Intelligence workstreams, including prompt-writing best practices to focus the observation summarizations of AI assistantsStrong research experience and familiarity with the process for developing consumer, category & cultural insightsStrong storytelling experience through the creation and presentation of compelling slide decksAbility to translate business needs into strategic social intelligence frameworks that can be executed & replicated across a large organizationFamiliarity with foresight use cases, identifying and analyzing trend signals from social media that ladder up to larger cultural movements or consumer behavior shiftsUnderstanding of the social media landscape, dynamics of community interaction, social best practices, and digital analytics toolsStrong communication and interpersonal skillsAbility to execute multiple projects at once across various stakeholder teams throughout a large organization
ADDITIONAL PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

Familiarity with experimentation and A/B testing of social/digital content executionsFamiliarity with Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager for website analyticsFamiliarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud and its analytics functionalitiesFamiliarity with Power BI to create and visualize data from disparate data sets 
Salary: $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 per year

Bonus Eligibility: Yes

Additional selections may be made for other organizational divisions and/or units within the duty location(s) listed above.

Duties

Serving in this role allows for you to play a pivotal role in advancing the agency's mission by apply expertise in geospatial program management, data modeling, exploitation and analysis, project coordination, and communication. This position starts at a salary of $121,785.00 (GS-13, Step 1) to $158,322.00 (GS-13, Step 10). GS Salary: Visit this link to view the locality pay tables by geographic area. As a Management and Program Analyst, typical duties include: Managing and supporting geospatial program activities, including GIS projects, applications, software guidance, standards, policies, procedures, and instructions to ensure alignment with mission objectives and organizational business goals. Developing project plans, proposals, requirements, budget inputs, and contracting documentation for major geospatial initiatives, business process changes, and program transitions. Analyzing, evaluating, and improving geospatial business processes, workflows, managerial practices, operational procedures, and administrative controls to increase program effectiveness and support evolving mission requirements. Coordinating with program managers, planners, liaisons, developers, data scientists, contractors, external partners, and geospatial subject matter experts to support cross-organizational GIS initiatives, resolve issues, and facilitate information sharing. For employees detailed or temporarily promoted for less than one year, the permanent duty location is considered the duty location of record for commuting area purposes.

Qualifications

Coordinating with internal and external stakeholders, including program managers, technical staff, contractors, partner organizations, or subject matter experts, to support geospatial initiatives and resolve program issues. rows.title: Business Development Analyst (Entry Talent Accelerator Program - Jan / Feb 2027)
rows.descriptionText:
The Company You’ll Join: Founded in 2016 to bring rigorous research and analytics to early careers and recruiting leaders, Veris Insights has grown to serve thousands of Heads of Talent, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, and Early Careers from over 300 Fortune 500 organizations. Our team of 80+, including researchers, consultants, PhDs, analysts, and executive service directors, work daily to help members understand, deliberate, and solve their hardest challenges.
The Team You’ll Join: You will join an existing Entry Talent Accelerator Program (ETA) cohort, a high-performance early-career development program designed for ambitious individuals looking to accelerate their growth in client-facing and revenue-generating environments.
This role is a full-time position beginning in Jan/Feb 2027 for graduating seniors.
As a Business Development Analyst, you will sit within our Growth Division and serve as one of the first points of contact for senior Talent Acquisition and University Recruiting leaders interested in Veris Insights' work. Through strategic outreach and insights-driven conversations, you will help generate interest in our memberships (ongoing partnerships that give organizations access to our research and advisory teams) while developing communication, advisory, and executive-facing skills foundational to long-term career growth at the firm.
This is an outbound growth and business development role centered around high-volume communication and strategic prospecting. Business Development Analysts spend a significant portion of their day conducting outbound outreach through phone, email, and LinkedIn, engaging senior leaders in thoughtful, data-informed conversations.
This role is best suited for individuals who are energized by frequent conversations with senior leaders and want their work measured, coached, and rewarded on results.
How You’ll Grow: The ETA Program is a structured, 12-18 month development program built around the Business Development Analyst role. The outreach, conversations, and objections you work through every day are where the skills below are built, and the program pairs that experience with a dedicated mentor, structured coaching, and regular feedback.
Through the program, you will develop:
Public Speaking & Executive Presence: Build confidence and fluency in high-pressure communication environments through coaching, repetition, and real-time feedback.
Consultative Advisory Skills: Learn how to identify executive priorities, build credibility quickly, and guide strategic conversations with senior leaders.
Negotiation & Influence: Develop the ability to navigate high-stakes conversations with confidence, professionalism, and strong interpersonal judgement.
Data Interpretation & Insight Delivery: Learn how to quickly interpret research and data to support real-time, insight-driven advisory conversations.
The program is designed to build the foundational skills of a working professional and prepare participants for client-facing and revenue-generating roles across the firm. Progression through the program is based on individual performance against defined milestones, and placement afterward is based on business need at the time.
Your Character:
Incisiveness. You quickly identify priorities, connect ideas, and thoughtfully diagnose challenges.
Executive Presence. You communicate with confidence, professionalism, warmth, and credibility across a wide range of audiences.
Results Orientation. You are motivated by performance, growth, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Intellectual Curiosity. You enjoy learning quickly, asking thoughtful questions, and building expertise in complex topics.
Empathy & Service Orientation. You genuinely care about the people you work with and strive to build trust in every interaction.
Key Responsibilities: Direct Outreach & Pipeline GenerationExecute high-volume, multi-channel outbound outreach through phone, email, and LinkedIn to generate qualified pipelineWork toward defined activity, prospecting, and pipeline-generation goals, using performance data and strategy to improve resultsGenerate interest and build relationships with senior Talent Acquisition and University Recruiting leaders
Key Responsibilities: Growth Strategy & Partnership SupportPartner with Account Advisors to prioritize accounts, identify the right senior stakeholders, and develop tailored prospecting strategiesAnalyze trends and collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing and Revenue OperationsMaintain accurate records, activity tracking, and pipeline support within Salesforce
Key Responsibilities: ETA Program ParticipationCollaborate with your mentor to build and execute an individualized growth planCollaborate with your cohort peers on team initiatives that improve outreach, messaging, and pipeline strategyIdentify firmwide opportunities and present strategic recommendations to leadership
RequirementsBachelor's degree with an expected graduation date between May and December 2026Internship, part-time, or other experience in business development, sales development, recruiting, fundraising, hospitality, customer success, or similar client-facing environments is a plusStrong communication skills and comfort operating in fast-paced environmentsDemonstrated curiosity, coachability, and learning agilityA proactive, solution-oriented mindsetFamiliarity with sales and prospecting tools such as Salesforce, Salesloft, ZoomInfo, or LinkedIn Sales Navigator is a plus
Compensation & BenefitsSalary: $60,000-$65,000 base salary, depending on qualifications, plus variable commission based on performanceHybrid Schedule: 3 days per week in our Washington, DC officeUnlimited PTO and monthly mental health daysMedical, dental, and vision coverage$1,000 annual wellness stipend401(k) with up to 4% employer matchPaid parental leave
Work AuthorizationApplicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future visa sponsorship. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider OPT/CPT holders.
Please keep in mind: Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds only apply to jobs when they meet 100% of the requirements vs. their majority counterparts, which apply at a much higher rate if they meet 50-60% of the requirements. So, with that being said, if you are interested in the role, we would love to hear how you can leverage your talents to be an awesome culture add.
Our Values & Culture, In Brief: Talent is in our DNA. It is what we study, who we serve, and the quality we most pride ourselves on internally. In order for our team members to be at their best, we provide individualized benefits and support. We believe a well-rounded and diverse team is the key to our success. To provide the widest range of experiences and perspectives in our member service and internal culture, we never discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status. Please let our recruiter know if there are any accommodations we can provide for you to ensure an equitable and comfortable recruitment process.
We highly value diversity, equity, and inclusion, and this shows up in everything we do. Our research has a significant focus on the experiences of candidates from diverse backgrounds. Internally, we have Employee Resource Groups for BIPOC and LGBTQ+ employees, and Affinity Groups to support women and neurodiversity. Furthermore, we’ve established a Diversity Council to promote a workplace environment that is safe, respectful, and inclusive for all and acts as an active partner to People Ops and Leadership in service of our broader firm-wide DEI goals.

rows.title: Senior Analyst, Activation (Amazon Ads)

We do this by acting as clients’ agency of record, as their in-house team, or some hybrid of the two – and by harnessing data and technology across all paid digital media and data-driven CRM channels.

Kepler prides itself on being a great place to work. In fact, we’re proud to share that AdAge recognized Kepler among the Best Place to Work in 2022, validating our investment in our team and our clients.
